Cyril: Clawing back the billions

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We all wonder what our president is doing right? But here's the answer: he's using civil litigation to claw back the billions and fighting corruption

Unique Selling Point:
So what has Ramaphosa done?
Summary:
1. rid of the rot and replaced them with competent office holders, as well as rebuilding institutions
2. A lot of action through civil proceedings (sequestration, asset seizure and civil claims)
3. Progress has been made with some state-owned enterprises, although most of the covid 19 corruption seems to take place at the provincial and local gov level (we'll use examples of eskom, transnet and NPA)
4. Ramaphosa has put the state on a new trajectory, he is trying to ensure that the ANC follows.

Eskom retrieved 1 billion from Mckinsey, 150m from Deloitte, they have cancelled coal contracts worth R3.7 billion as well a R14 billion oil supply contract, and other contracts are being investigated. The SIU in august launched proceedings to recover R3.8 billion from 12 individuals connected to eskom. And the SIU are clawing back R400 million from two contracts connected with eskom and transnet for computer software.
At Transnet the South China Rail has repaid R618 million, R1,168 billion has been recovered from Gupta entities and assets worth R232 million from a former Gupta associate have been frozen. Prasa has been put under administration.
At the land bank there have been people who have gone to jail for fraud.
At the NPA, Ramaphosa dismissed its national director and the president appointed a commission to investigate the deputy directors - which were both fired. And now new permanent deputy's have been appointed, and Shamila Batohi has taken office after being recruited from The Hague.
In his SONA speech in February, Ramaphosa announced that a special unit would be created within the NPA to prosecute state capture cases: with skills from "within government and the private sector." Hermione Cronje has not been appointed outside the NPA to head this unit, and R38 million has been allocated from Treasury for this unit, and R25 million has been allocated for appoint private sector practitioners and R102 million to fill vacancies - 800 posts were advertised in February 2020. Ramaphosa after consulting top lawyer Wim Trengrove revoked the appointments of five senior prosecutors.
In July 2020 regulations on the Zondo commission were changed allowing the NPA to use evidence from the commission in criminal prosecution.
At the ANC's National Executive Council (NEC) they resolved to urgently establish a permanent multidisciplinary agency to deal with all cases of white collar crime, organized crime and corruption.

The SIU and Special Tribunal - their mandate is to recover public money through civil claims - they do not prosecute. But the SIU can refer a case to NPA to prosecute. * Criminal cases require "beyond reasonable doubt" - while civil claims require the less strenuous test of "on a balance of probabilities." To speed up civil litigation, President Ramaphosa created the Special Tribunal to adjudicate civil proceedings - operation from 1 oct 2019 - chaired by 8 judged and lead by Judge Thami Makhanya. Currently 22 cases are before the tribunal - like luxury care purchases, dodgy scholar transport claims and inflated gov contracts. In 2 cases the tribunal ruled that pension of suspects be frozen, giving the SIU the opportunity to seize the money, meaning resigning and running with ones pension has become more difficult. The SIU has R14.7 billion in cases it wishes to submit to tribunal.

AFU (which focus on 10 specific crimes incl fraud, cash smuggling, human trafficking, counterfeit fraud and drug related offences). Although they were deliberately restrained in Zuma era, and now has a new lease on life. It reported last years it recovered nearly R2 billion from economic crimes compared with only R180 million the previous year. Over the past 5 years they've recovered R11.8 billion in 2707 cases. For eg. two weeks ago they seized the bank accounts of R700,000 siphoned off UIF money meant for underemployed workers.

Summary:
10 months after coming into power the president had instituted the Nugent commission of inquiry, which made way for a new commissioner Edward Kieswetter and several other experts coming back to SARS.
He then instituted the Mpati commission at the PIC, and a special team under Judge Yvonne Mokgoro is implementing the recommendations along with a new board. This lead to summons' being issued to past board members.
And now several investigative agencies are being pulled together to investigate the alleged PPE tender corruption.
Prosecutions:
As the wheels of justice turn slowly, they are turning. Zuma has suffered a number of setbacks in various courts.
The Hawks are investigating 250 cases of municipal fraud of which 93 are already in court.
In June 2002 - 9 suspects were arrested for the VBS Mutual Bank saga - and one of them as turned state witness to secure convictions. 5 of them were sequestrated and their assets seized to repay moneys to the bank, and 2 were declared delinquent and cannot be company directors again. At least consequences are following, even before jail sentences.
Dudu Myeni has also been declared a delinquent director after SAA and the Muhlathuzi water board.



Further information:
We are going to have to decide on and discuss the experts... and how we visually tell the story. Going to be a challenge.

Script:



South Africans have been united in their rage towards corruption...and frustrated at the perceived lack of accountability.
The recent Personal Protective Equipment scandal grabbed headlines...shock-waves reaching even the most patriotic citizen – President Cyril Ramaphosa.
Ramaphosa: I’ve often asked myself what gets into somebody’s head that a mask can ordinarily cost R2-R3 is now sold at R90? That is not only wrong, that is criminal.
Ramaphosa has staked his legacy on holding the corrupt to account.
UPSOUNDS: corruption, corruption, corruption… we have drawn a line in the sand when it comes to corruption!
That line in the sand has formed the foundation of Ramaphosa’s plan to use civil litigation to claw back billions of Rands lost to corruption. The State Investigative Unit or SIU have tackled these priority cases, says spokesperson Kaizer Khanyago.
K: We collect cash in terms of getting the recoveries from people. We freeze people's assets so that we ultimately get those assets sold we block the methods from before the payments are done. And that for me is still a saving on our side.
The Zondo Commission of Inquiry into State Capture has heard testimony of corruption amounting to tens of billions over a decade at power utility Eskom.
IN AUGUST, THE SIU LAUNCHED PROCEEDINGS TO RECOVER R3.8 BILLION FROM 12 INDIVIDUALS CONNECTED TO ESKOM.
AUDITING FIRM DELOITTE AGREED TO PAY BACK 150MILLION AFTER THEY WERE ACCUSED OF IRREGULAR TENDER PROCESSES
ESKOM CANCELLED PROBLEMATIC SEVERAL CONTRACTS, R3.7 BILLION RANDS WORTH OF COAL CONTRACTS, AS WELL A R14 BILLION OIL SUPPLY CONTRACT, OTHERS CONTRACTS ARE UNDER INVESTIGATION.

K: The the main function of the SIU used to investigate malpractice maladministration and malfeasance in government institutions.
The Zondo Commission has also been presented with evidence of state capture allegations amounting to roughly 3 billion Rand in relation to the Gupta family and the supply of trains at Transnet.
AT TRANSNET, SOUTH CHINA RAIL HAS REPAID R618 MILLION,
R1,168 BILLION HAS BEEN RECOVERED FROM GUPTA ENTITIES
AND ASSETS WORTH R232 MILLION FROM A FORMER GUPTA ASSOCIATE HAVE BEEN FROZEN.

C: The president has come out saying that he stands firmly behind anti-corruption. Has that changed the way the SIU has been working?
K: ever since he came in all the reports on almost all the reports were publicized were given to the institutions.
The SIU isn't a body that can prosecute, so it hands its evidence over to the NPA. South Africans want to see Orange Overalls...and Ramaphosa created an investigating directorate to add to the corruption-busting arsenal. In his Sona Speech in February 2019,
IN HIS SONA SPEECH IN FEBRUARY, 2019/LAST YEAR, RAMAPHOSA ANNOUNCED THAT A SPECIAL UNIT WOULD BE CREATED WITHIN THE NPA TO PROSECUTE STATE CAPTURE CASES.
Ramaphosa: Now the processes surrounding corruption are being undertaken by the siu, by SARS and all the agency’s together in what we call the fusion centre. We are looking at much broader measures to tackle corruption in general from strengthening and better resourcing existing agencies to establishing a permanent multidisciplinary entity to ensure more effective detection and prosecution.
Accepting responsibility for this unit is a highly experienced advocate, who came up through the asset forfeiture unit - Hermione Cronje. Appointed by Ramaphosa, Cronje fiercely guards the Directorate’s independence, which decides who to prosecute, and even has the power to effect arrests.
H: We have 3 focus areas: Which deals with state capture or corruption in the criminal justice system, so the police, the NPA, the state security agency. Then investigations into SOEs like eskom and transnet and then have the third And then high level public/private corruption.
The Directorate has been allocated R38 million from Treasury.
H: We were able to appoint our first investigator on contract two months ago.
Cronje now has 16 prosecutors and 22 investigators who have executed 17 arrests... and counting, in the past few weeks.
H: The challenge of doing this work in many of these cases - Estina, Bosasa, Panday, Mado - is that these cases should have been prosecuted 10 years ago, they weren’t, and that automatically implicates players in the criminal justice system. We are investigating in an environment that is still fairly contaminated and oxic. But, i'm absolutely excited that it's now becoming visible, the work that we have done, and i'm confident that when these cases appear, you’ll see the effort and quality of work that went into bringing these cases into court.
Even while our cameras rolled, Cronje received requests to sign off on charge sheets for the next number of prosecutions.
LINK: IN JULY THIS YEAR, REGULATIONS AT THE ZONDO COMMISSION WERE CHANGED ALLOWING THE NPA TO USE EVIDENCE FROM THE COMMISSION IN CRIMINAL PROSECUTION.
The rules have allowed us to access the information but also the personnel who have been working on those cases
Ramphosa’s team say he has pursued the strategy of civil litigation first, because criminal cases require evidence ‘beyond all reasonable doubt’ while civil claims require a less strenuous test... ‘on a balance of probabilities’.
H: So the SIU and the Asset Forfeiture Unit can bring civil proceedings; the SIU can set aside contracts and get ‘Just and Equitable’ relief from courts, the AFU can recover the proceeds of corruption, and the instruments of corruption through civil proceedings.
LINK: AT ESKOM, 1 BILLION WAS RETRIEVED BY THE ASSET FORFEITURE UNIT AFTER MANAGEMENT- FEES PAID TO A US FIRM WERE FOUND TO BE UNLAWFUL
H: We take people to court and we have to show on the criminal standard, ‘Beyond Reasonable Doubt’ - the much more stringent test, because the consequence of doing so will have people spending time in jail for hopefully a very very long time.
To fast-track civil litigation, Ramaphosa added a special tribunal to the SIU, which allows 8 judges to adjudicate civil proceedings.
K: That is why you see the processes now are rolling very quickly when we want to for example freeze the contract of somebody who just resigned and quickly went in to get out and get the money that the pension money.
Experts have tried to calculate the financial damage of state capture.
L: There's no number. We all tried to figure out but the estimates of sea range between - on top of 4 trillion rand.
Economist Lumkile Mondi of the Wits University School of Economics and Finance says investors in South Africa need to see that their money is not wasted on corruption.
L: President Ramaphosa had an understanding of how deep the problems were, and was allowing the process through the cabinet to continue. But the core of the problem is within the ANC, for example where Ace Makgashule, whose name keeps coming up all the time. And yet we haven't seen him coming to the commission.
Political analyst Prof. Tinyiko Maluleke OF the university of Pretoria, is sceptical of the progress...as factions within the ANC are fighting back against Ramaphosa’s cause.
Maluleke: Let's face it there is no Cyril Ramaphosa without the ANC. can he as an individual change the direction of the Titanic? The rest of the ANC itself is at sixes and sevens, we splash out the news that we are suspending so-and-so, we’re asking them to step aside and then a few months later we bring some of them back. Zandile gumede, the ethikwini mayor, we are told she is incompetent, then after which we are told no she is becoming a member of the provincial legislature, double her salary.
Analysts have reservations on the ANC’s integrity commission meting out consequences...one of which may be a loss of party membership.
Tinyiko: As South Africans we should dis-invest from the factions of the ANC because the ANC can't investigate itself.
LINK: THE WHEELS OF JUSTICE DO TURN SLOWLY, BUT THEY ARE TURNING. THE HAWKS ARE INVESTIGATING 250 CASES OF MUNICIPAL FRAUD OF WHICH NEARLY 100 ARE IN COURT. IN JUNE, 9 SUSPECTS WERE ARRESTED FOR THE VBS MUTUAL BANK SAGA.
C: On your Web site you say it stated there that that that there is a war on corruption.
K: It means we are going to do our work without favor or fear.
H: We've already had threats, we've had sort of incursions. This is not work you do for money, but because you're passionate about it.

Analysts have reservations on the ANC’s integrity commission meting out consequences...one of which may be a loss of party membership. Tinyiko: As South Africans we should dis-invest from the factions of the ANC because the ANC can't investigate itself. LINK: THE WHEELS OF JUSTICE DO TURN SLOWLY, BUT THEY ARE TURNING. THE HAWKS ARE INVESTIGATING 250 CASES OF MUNICIPAL FRAUD OF WHICH NEARLY 100 ARE IN COURT. IN JUNE, 9 SUSPECTS WERE ARRESTED FOR THE VBS MUTUAL BANK SAGA. C: On your Web site you say it stated there that that that there is a war on corruption. K: It means we are going to do our work without favor or fear. H: We've already had threats, we've had sort of incursions. This is not work you do for money, but because you're passionate about it.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We all wonder what our president is doing right? But here's the answer: he's using civil litigation to claw back the billions and fighting corruption
metadata.Unique Selling Point: So what has Ramaphosa done? Summary: 1. rid of the rot and replaced them with competent office holders, as well as rebuilding institutions 2. A lot of action through civil proceedings (sequestration, asset seizure and civil claims) 3. Progress has been made with some state-owned enterprises, although most of the covid 19 corruption seems to take place at the provincial and local gov level (we'll use examples of eskom, transnet and NPA) 4. Ramaphosa has put the state on a new trajectory, he is trying to ensure that the ANC follows. Eskom retrieved 1 billion from Mckinsey, 150m from Deloitte, they have cancelled coal contracts worth R3.7 billion as well a R14 billion oil supply contract, and other contracts are being investigated. The SIU in august launched proceedings to recover R3.8 billion from 12 individuals connected to eskom. And the SIU are clawing back R400 million from two contracts connected with eskom and transnet for computer software. At Transnet the South China Rail has repaid R618 million, R1,168 billion has been recovered from Gupta entities and assets worth R232 million from a former Gupta associate have been frozen. Prasa has been put under administration. At the land bank there have been people who have gone to jail for fraud. At the NPA, Ramaphosa dismissed its national director and the president appointed a commission to investigate the deputy directors - which were both fired. And now new permanent deputy's have been appointed, and Shamila Batohi has taken office after being recruited from The Hague. In his SONA speech in February, Ramaphosa announced that a special unit would be created within the NPA to prosecute state capture cases: with skills from "within government and the private sector." Hermione Cronje has not been appointed outside the NPA to head this unit, and R38 million has been allocated from Treasury for this unit, and R25 million has been allocated for appoint private sector practitioners and R102 million to fill vacancies - 800 posts were advertised in February 2020. Ramaphosa after consulting top lawyer Wim Trengrove revoked the appointments of five senior prosecutors. In July 2020 regulations on the Zondo commission were changed allowing the NPA to use evidence from the commission in criminal prosecution. At the ANC's National Executive Council (NEC) they resolved to urgently establish a permanent multidisciplinary agency to deal with all cases of white collar crime, organized crime and corruption. The SIU and Special Tribunal - their mandate is to recover public money through civil claims - they do not prosecute. But the SIU can refer a case to NPA to prosecute. * Criminal cases require "beyond reasonable doubt" - while civil claims require the less strenuous test of "on a balance of probabilities." To speed up civil litigation, President Ramaphosa created the Special Tribunal to adjudicate civil proceedings - operation from 1 oct 2019 - chaired by 8 judged and lead by Judge Thami Makhanya. Currently 22 cases are before the tribunal - like luxury care purchases, dodgy scholar transport claims and inflated gov contracts. In 2 cases the tribunal ruled that pension of suspects be frozen, giving the SIU the opportunity to seize the money, meaning resigning and running with ones pension has become more difficult. The SIU has R14.7 billion in cases it wishes to submit to tribunal. AFU (which focus on 10 specific crimes incl fraud, cash smuggling, human trafficking, counterfeit fraud and drug related offences). Although they were deliberately restrained in Zuma era, and now has a new lease on life. It reported last years it recovered nearly R2 billion from economic crimes compared with only R180 million the previous year. Over the past 5 years they've recovered R11.8 billion in 2707 cases. For eg. two weeks ago they seized the bank accounts of R700,000 siphoned off UIF money meant for underemployed workers.
metadata.Summary: 10 months after coming into power the president had instituted the Nugent commission of inquiry, which made way for a new commissioner Edward Kieswetter and several other experts coming back to SARS. He then instituted the Mpati commission at the PIC, and a special team under Judge Yvonne Mokgoro is implementing the recommendations along with a new board. This lead to summons' being issued to past board members. And now several investigative agencies are being pulled together to investigate the alleged PPE tender corruption. Prosecutions: As the wheels of justice turn slowly, they are turning. Zuma has suffered a number of setbacks in various courts. The Hawks are investigating 250 cases of municipal fraud of which 93 are already in court. In June 2002 - 9 suspects were arrested for the VBS Mutual Bank saga - and one of them as turned state witness to secure convictions. 5 of them were sequestrated and their assets seized to repay moneys to the bank, and 2 were declared delinquent and cannot be company directors again. At least consequences are following, even before jail sentences. Dudu Myeni has also been declared a delinquent director after SAA and the Muhlathuzi water board.
